rules.statement: When a change amends an accepted architecture decision record, mark the relationship in the amended record's Status line and index entry ("amended by ADR-N") and list it on the new record's amends/refines line, rather than rewriting the old record's Decision text; don't ask for the old Decision text to be reworded.
rules.why: Decision records relate to each other through Status metadata, so the old text stays as the historical decision and the new record carries the change.
rules.check: In a diff that adds a decision record superseding part of an older one, confirm the older record's Status and index row name the new record; don't report the unchanged Decision text of the amended record as a contradiction.

rules.statement: Put build logic that several Dockerfiles or pipelines share, such as stamping a version into a file, in one script that each of them runs, and make the script fail when its rewrite didn't produce the expected content.
rules.why: Duplicated snippets must be changed in several places, and a text substitution that stops matching fails silently, so the image keeps the old version while its tag claims the new one.
rules.check: Look for the same RUN/sed/validation block copied into more than one Dockerfile or workflow, and for in-place file rewrites (sed, regex replace) with no check afterwards that the file now holds the intended value.

rules.statement: Don't suggest passing the version to `dotnet publish` as an MSBuild property (`-p:Version`, `-p:AssemblyInformationalVersion`) when the build uses Nerdbank.GitVersioning with `NBGV_GitEngine=Disabled`; there the version has to be written into `version.json`.
rules.why: With the git engine disabled, Nerdbank.GitVersioning ignores those properties and reads only `version.json`.
rules.check: Before recommending an MSBuild version property, check whether the build sets `NBGV_GitEngine=Disabled` and takes its version from `version.json`.

rules.statement: In a GitHub Actions workflow, define a message or value that several steps of a job use once, as a job-level `env` variable, and refer to it from each step instead of repeating the literal.
rules.why: Copies of the same text drift apart from each other and from the documentation they point to.
rules.check: Look for the same string literal (hint messages, URLs, names) written out in more than one step of a job.

rules.statement: Write an explanatory comment once, above the first place it applies, instead of repeating it word for word above each similar step or block.
rules.why: Repeated comments make a reader wonder whether the commented steps differ.
rules.check: Look for identical comments placed above several sibling steps or blocks in the same file.
